Fit a latent transition model

Source: R/transitions.R
lta.Rd

Latent transition analysis describes stability and change in latent states across repeated occasions. The states (profiles) are patterns in continuous or discrete indicators; transition probabilities give the chance of staying in a state or moving to another between successive occasions. lta() estimates the measurement and transition parameters jointly.

By default the chain is first order and time-homogeneous: the state at an occasion depends on the state before it, with the same transition matrix at every occasion. The measurement parameters are shared across occasions and across group classes, so a state means the same thing throughout and group classes differ only in their initial distribution and transitions. Options add covariate-dependent transitions, occasion-specific transitions or measurement, second-order dependence, a mover-stayer class, sampling weights and ordinal or count indicators; any of these changes the result class (see Value).

Usage

lta(
  data,
  vars,
  id,
  n_profiles,
  time,
  n_group_classes = 1L,
  variance_model = c("varying", "equal"),
  n_starts = 10L,
  max_iter = 5000L,
  tol = 1e-10,
  min_variance = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  missing = c("error", "fiml"),
  covariance_model = c("diagonal", "full"),
  categorical = character(),
  min_probability = 1e-10,
  occasions = c("observed", "grid"),
  select_start = c("likelihood", "converged"),
  transitions = c("homogeneous", "occasion"),
  transition_covariates = character(),
  initial_covariates = character(),
  measurement = c("invariant", "occasion"),
  order = 1L,
  model = NULL,
  mover_stayer = FALSE,
  weights = NULL,
  ordinal = character(),
  count = character(),
  count_model = c("poisson", "negative_binomial"),
  count_dispersion = c("varying", "equal"),
  drop_empty = TRUE,
  search = c("kmeans", "emEM"),
  n_screen = NULL,
  acceleration = c("squarem", "none"),
  cores = 1L
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with the indicators and the group identifier.

vars

Names of the indicator columns. Those not named in categorical, ordinal or count are continuous.

id

Name of the group identifier column (character, factor or numeric, without missing values). Required.

n_profiles

Number of profiles, at least two.

time

Column giving each row's occasion within its group. Required; values must be unique within a group and sort in their intended order (numbers numerically, factors by level, text alphabetically, so "T2", "T10" is refused; use a factor or zero-pad).

n_group_classes

Number of group classes (default 1). More than one fits a mixture of transition models over the units.

variance_model

"varying" (default): each profile has its own variances or covariance matrix; "equal": one shared by all profiles.

n_starts

Number of EM starts (default 10). The first is deterministic (Ward's clustering), the rest random; the reported start need not have converged, so check converged. See Starts and convergence under multilpa().

max_iter

Maximum EM updates per start (default 5000). The fit warns when its reported start stopped short. max_iter = 0 evaluates the starting values without updating them and reports converged = FALSE.

tol

Convergence tolerance (default 1e-10): EM stops when a step changes the log likelihood by no more than tol times the number of observed indicator values.

min_variance

Lower bound on every variance (on every covariance eigenvalue under full covariance). NULL (default) uses 1e-6 times the smallest sample variance of the continuous indicators, on the scale fitted; a number is an absolute bound in squared indicator units. An estimate at the bound is a boundary solution and warns.

seed

Optional integer seed. The caller's random-number state is restored on exit.

missing

"error" (default) rejects missing indicator values; "fiml" maximizes the observed-data likelihood under MAR. Covariates must be complete either way. See Occasions without data.

covariance_model

"diagonal" (default): the indicators are independent within a profile; "full": within-profile covariances are estimated.

categorical

Indicators modelled by profile-specific response probabilities over their observed categories, the latent class measurement model. Binary, ordered and unordered indicators share this parameterization. Naming a subset of vars fits a mixed-mode model.

min_probability

Lower bound on every categorical response probability (default 1e-10).

occasions

How a group's occasions are placed on the transition grid. "observed" (default) numbers each group's own rows consecutively, so a transition always links two adjacent rows. "grid" places them on the grid of every position seen in the data, so a group that skips a position still makes a transition across the gap and contributes no measurement at it. The two agree when every group is observed at every position. Under either, a group's first row is its first occasion: occasion-specific transitions and measurement count occasions from each group's own start, not from the first position in the data.

select_start

Which start is reported. "likelihood" (default): the highest log likelihood, preferring a converged start among those tied within tolerance. "converged": the best converged start when there is one. summary() and get_results(fit, "starts") report every start.

transitions

"homogeneous" (default): one transition matrix for every occasion. "occasion": a separate matrix for each move (occasion 1 to 2, 2 to 3, and so on). See Occasions without data.

transition_covariates

Columns whose values shift the transition probabilities through a multinomial logit per origin profile (the log odds of moving to each other profile rather than staying). A column may change over occasions; the value at the destination occasion is used. Factors are expanded to indicator columns after dropping unused levels. With occasions = "grid", a skipped position has no row to read the covariates from and is refused: use "observed", or add the skipped rows with their covariate values and missing indicators under FIML.

initial_covariates

Columns that shift the initial profile distribution (a multinomial logit, last profile as reference), read at each group's first occasion. Factors are expanded as for transition_covariates.

measurement

"invariant" (default) keeps the profiles' means, variances and response probabilities equal across occasions; "occasion" estimates them separately at each occasion.

order

1 (default) or 2. With 2, the profile at each occasion from the third on depends on the profiles at the two previous occasions; the first transition stays first order.

model

A covariance structure as multilpa() takes it (mclust's codes, such as "VVI"). A multilpa_transitions fit gives standard errors for EEI, VVI, EEE and VVV only; a multilpa_lta fit (see Value) gives them for every structure.

mover_stayer

TRUE adds a class of stayers: units that never change profile (identity transitions) with their own initial distribution, the mover-stayer model. n_group_classes then counts the mover classes; the stayer class is reported as "stayers".

weights

Name of a column holding one sampling weight per id (constant over its occasions): pseudo maximum likelihood with sandwich standard errors, as under multilpa(). The model-implied "transitions" and "initial" tables then average the units with their weights.

ordinal, count, count_model, count_dispersion

Ordinal and count indicators, as under multilpa(); with measurement = "occasion" their parameters are estimated per occasion. Read with get_results(fit, "ordinal") and get_results(fit, "count_means").

drop_empty

TRUE (default) leaves rows with no observed indicator, and groups made only of such rows, out of the sample sizes, entropies and classification tables, as Mplus does, keeping their rows with NA in the assignment tables. FALSE counts them in the entropies, the tables and the number of groups, so the criteria over groups and those using the entropy change; the number of rows in the individual-level criteria stays the informative rows for profile and class models. For transition models, FALSE also counts all positive-weight rows in the individual-level BIC. Estimation is the same either way; fits with different settings are not compared.

search

"kmeans" (default) or "emEM", as under multilpa(). Unlike multilpa(), lta() does not pick the default by covariance structure.

n_screen

For search = "emEM" only, the size of the screened pool (default five times n_starts, at least n_starts).

acceleration

"squarem" (default) accelerates EM with SQUAREM, as under multilpa(); "none" runs plain EM.

cores

Number of processor cores for the starts (default 1); with seed the result is identical to one core. To fit several models, give cores to enumerate_classes() instead.

Value

A multilpa_transitions object with means, variances (and covariances or response_probabilities), initial_probabilities (group classes by profiles), transition_probabilities (profiles by profiles by group classes, rows indexing the profile moved from), group_probabilities, the posterior matrices and classifications, log_likelihood, the information criteria, the starts table and the convergence history. get_results() returns its tables, parameter_inference() Wald or bootstrap standard errors and bootstrap_lrt() compares nested fits.

With transitions = "occasion", transition_covariates, initial_covariates, measurement = "occasion", order = 2, mover_stayer = TRUE, weights, ordinal or count, the result is a multilpa_lta object: its tables are transition and initial logit coefficients with Wald standard errors, model-implied transition probabilities per occasion (with an estimated column), profiles per occasion and the assignments.

Profile labels are arbitrary and not comparable across fits without alignment.

Occasions without data

A transition the data never observe is not estimated. A profile that no unit of a group class occupies before the unit's last occasion has no move out of it: its row of the transition matrix is uniform by construction, flagged estimated = FALSE, not counted in n_parameters, AIC or BIC, and reported with a warning. On a multilpa_transitions fit, get_results(fit, "transitions", estimated = FALSE) lists such rows. Nonzero origins with fewer than one expected outgoing move trigger a weak- support warning. Transition tables show origin_expected_count and supported; Wald inference is withheld. These nonzero rows remain formally estimated and counted in the criteria: this is a support diagnostic, not a declaration of structural non-identification. Homogeneous rows pool support across their applicable moves; occasion- specific rows use that occasion's count. The averaged second-order table reports the total count, but supported is false if any separately fitted occasion has fewer than one expected outgoing move.

Under FIML, three more things are unidentified and flagged the same way: under transitions = "occasion", a move into an occasion at which no row observes an indicator (after the last observed occasion it does not enter the likelihood; before it, only through its product with the move out); under order = 2, the second-order logits when nothing is observed from occasion 3 on; under measurement = "occasion", the measurement block of an empty occasion.

For second-order occasion-specific chains, an empty interior occasion does not use the first-order product rule: remaining logits stay counted and the parameter count is an upper bound. A second-order fit's first-order table describes only the move into occasion 2. The second-order table averages over groups and applicable occasions, with move-frequency weights.

Short panels and bootstrap support

Without initial or transition covariates, two occasions cannot identify multiple group classes or a separate stayer class. Three occasions cannot identify multiple freely moving group classes with occasion-specific transitions, or multiple classes in a second-order chain. These specifications are refused; convergence cannot resolve an identification ridge. Specifications whose chain coordinates outnumber the latent path probabilities are refused as well.

Bootstrap resamples whose occasions or factor levels change the coefficient set are recorded as failed resamples. Intervals use retained resamples only, with a warning and recorded reasons, and are conditional on those resamples supporting the requested coefficients. With drop_empty = FALSE, both engines count every positive-weight row in the individual BIC; the default counts rows that observe an indicator. Initial or transition probabilities at the effective numerical bound also set boundary = TRUE in both engines; bootstrap likelihood-ratio tests refuse such inputs, as they already do for general transition fits.

See also

get_results() for the transition table and the assignments; plot_transitions() and plot_sequences(); multilpa() for the cross-sectional model whose measurement this one shares; enumerate_classes() to compare numbers of profiles.

Examples

# Model engagement transitions across each student's course sequence.
fit <- lta(
  course_engagement,
  vars = c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read", "forum_post", "attendance"),
  id = "student", n_profiles = 2, time = "sequence", n_starts = 2, seed = 1
)
get_results(fit, what = "transitions")
